answer: A cedar gate charges one burned tax per identity: each agent burns 40 credits before earning, never refunded. At the wharf, each berth is priced separately, so a second identity cannot reuse the first receipt and pays 40 again. The k-th fake adds exactly 40 credits, so 1,000 fakes cost 40,000 credits, a linear sunk cost with no bulk discount. A plume of copied receipts fails because each burn record binds one identity key and is checked before reward. An honest agent pays 40 once and keeps its share; tax rental fails when key, burn record, and work history do not match.
